name: fairy islands
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy islands form a folkloric motif. The western sea holds these enchanted isles, which often mark the Otherworld or Fairyland. These islands drift. They do not stay tied to one place or time. They surface at intervals onto different sites. One such island rose every seven years off Rathlin O'Birne, southwest of it, near the shore of Donegal. A person could settle that land and draw it fully into this world. One way was to land glowing embers on the island.

okr.objective: Fairy islands are enchanted isles of the Otherworld that drift in the west.
key_results: Fairy islands drift and appear at different sites.
One such island surfaced near Rathlin O'Birne, off Donegal.
A person could draw the island into this world.
Live embers first had to be landed upon it.
